prompt: Let $B_r^{R_i}(v)$ be the radius-$r$ ball in $(V,R_i)$. In the merge-sequence convention allowing several merges per step, which quantity is the sequence’s radius-$r$ width?

answers.explanation: Count parts reached through resolved pairs, not vertices. Use the previous partition with the current resolved-pair set; the index offset prevents a large merge from hiding its cost.
A ball may contain many vertices in one part. Width counts intersected parts instead of vertices.
Only parts reached from a vertex within the radius count, not every current part.
The number of resolved pairs is not the local reachability width.
Using the new partition omits the required offset. A single large merge could collapse the measured count to one.
This measures the old resolved set and ignores pairs resolved immediately before the merge.
Reachability is in the resolved-pair graph, which includes resolved non-edges, not in the original graph.
Every vertex must satisfy the width bound; the best vertex cannot witness the maximum local complexity.
The sequence width is the worst stage, not the easiest stage.
Reaching one vertex of a part suffices. The ball need not contain the entire part.

sources.title: Dreier & Toruńczyk — Merge-width and First-Order Model Checking, Definitions 3.1–3.2 and §7 (June 2026 version)
